newsitem.title: USA: Apple COO Scalise quits, leaves for SIA.
newsitem.headline: Apple COO Scalise quits, leaves for SIA.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc's chief operating officer George Scalise said Tuesday he will resign from his position at the computer maker to become president of the Semiconductor Industry Association.

Scalise, who joined Apple a little over a year ago, is one of about a half-dozen top executives to leave Apple in the past three months as the computer maker struggles to cut costs and get sales going again.
Scalise said he is leaving Apple because he accomplished all the goals he set for himself.
Apple will eliminate the position of chief operating officer, he said.

"The main reason for leaving is that I had some objectives when I came here," including figuring out a way to manage the company's assets better, to get product development going again and to restructure the business, Scalise said. "That has largely been accomplished."
Scalise also said Apple has decided what to do with the Newton handheld computer, one of his tasks. He declined to say what the company plans to do with the product, but said, "Stay tuned."
Industry executives have been speculating that Apple may sell the Newton.
